summary: Camera-local JSON-RPC command catalog (HTTPS :443, POST /stok={token}/ds). Every call is {method, params}; params = {module: {section: data}} built from Module/Section enum strings (section 'null' collapses to {module: data}). Reads select sections via 'name' or 'table' lists. The app always batches calls in multipleRequest {params:{requests:[...]}} and gets result.responses[] with per-item error_code. Feature support is discovered via getAppComponentList (name/version). Covers device info, PTZ (move/step/stop/cruise/calibrate/info), presets, privacy (lens mask), day/night and night-vision modes, LED, manual alarm/siren/alarm config, motion/person/vehicle/pet detection, flip/rotation, audio volume, reboot, time/timezone, SD card, record plan, connection type, and error codes.

items.description: Single JSON-RPC request object. 'method' is the camelCase string from Method.java; 'params' is the Gson-serialized params object (normally a Wrappers object, see envelope.params_wrapper_serialization).

The app ALWAYS sends commands batched inside multipleRequest, even single commands: i6(req) wraps the Wrapper in a Wrappers list, j6(req) wraps one request in a list, k6(list) builds the multipleRequest. A desktop client can batch any number of the sub-requests below into one call. MultipleRequest also has an optional 'emptyProperty' Boolean (null in all observed builders, so it is omitted).

items.description: Response object. error_code 0 == success (Response.isSuccess()). 'method' echoes the request method. 'result' holds the payload (for get* calls it mirrors the request's {module:{section:...}} nesting).

items.description: How Method + Module + Section combine. A Request's params is a Wrappers (list of Wrapper(module, section, data)). Serializer: for each Wrapper, if section == 'null' (Section.EMPTY) then params[module] = data; otherwise params[module][section] = data, merging several Wrappers of the same module into one object. Module and Section strings are the enum .value strings (Module.java / Section.java). So: {'method': Method.value, 'params': {Module.value: {Section.value: data}}}.

items.description: Response 'result' parsing (wrapperListDeserializer): if result has no 'data' key and ANY top-level value is a primitive, the whole result is treated as one flat object (Wrapper(EMPTY,EMPTY,result)); if it contains 'responseData'/'forward' it is also kept flat; if it has a single key in Module.Singles it is wrapped as (key,key); otherwise every result[module][section] becomes a Wrapper whose type is looked up in TypeDispatcher(module,section). Practical rule for a client: try result[module][section] first, else treat result as flat.

items.description: Older public clients (pytapo) use generic method names 'get', 'set', 'do' with the module object at the top level (e.g. {'method':'get','device_info':{'name':['basic_info']}}). The 3.22.806 app never uses these: the Method enum has no 'get'/'set'/'do' entries; every call uses a specific camelCase method plus params. A new client should use the specific method names; the generic forms are listed only for compatibility with older firmware.

Size of the command vocabulary in the app: Method enum 807 method strings, Module enum 179 module keys, Section enum 600 section keys, ComponentType 212 component names. Only the subset a desktop client needs is specified in this file.

motorMove x_coord/y_coord are integer strings; the app sends multiples of 5/10/15 per tap. The absolute limits come from getPtzInfo x/y_start_angle..end_angle; the unit (degrees vs motor steps) is not stated in code.

getPtzInfo/motorMove/stopMove/getConnectionType results are parsed with typeCastFromWrappers (first wrapper), so fields can be either directly in result or under result.<module>.<section>; client must accept both. Needs live capture to confirm.

setSirenStatus is built with module msg_alarm (battery-cam repository iv0.p0) and module siren (camera hub u3). For wired cameras the app path is doManualAlarm start/stop; which siren module a given wired model accepts is unverified.
RecordPlanInfo monday..sunday are opaque strings; the HHMM-HHMM:type encoding is from public knowledge, not confirmed in APK code.
Speaker/mic volume range assumed 0-100; detection sensitivity range is per-model (capability.sensitivity_range). Motion digital_sensitivity levels 20/60/80 come from UI snapping code.
